Request Your Quote

The quote request form asks only for what we need to price the job properly. Fill in the required fields, attach drawings and photos if you have them, and press send. Every request is read by a person, not an automated system.

Use the photo upload for clear pictures of each side of the part, and add anything unusual in the project details box, such as a tight deadline, a matching colour from an earlier job or parts that arrive in pieces.

blocks.text: A clear photo saves more time than any other field. It lets us see rust, old paint and welds before we price the work, so your quote for powder coating matches the part that actually arrives.
What to Send for an Accurate Price
Send part measurements, part quantity, the metal, the finish you want and one or two photos. With those five details we can usually price a job straight away, without a follow-up call.

Measure the longest length, the widest point and the height, including anything that sticks out. For the colour, give the colour code if you have one, such as a RAL number, or describe the look you want and we will suggest options. Note any masking requirements, such as threads, mounting faces or contact points that must stay bare. If the part has old paint or rust, mention it, because removal changes the powder coating estimate. For unusual or very heavy items, a sample part or a drawing helps us give a firm figure rather than a range. The more complete your request, the faster and more accurate your quote will be. A complete powder coating quote request rarely needs a second round of questions, and that keeps your job moving.
How Quoting Works, Step by Step

Quoting follows five steps: you send the request, we review it, we send a written estimate, you approve the job, then parts come in for coating. The table shows what happens at each step and how long it usually takes.

blocks.text: Our quote turnaround depends on how much detail arrives with the request. Complete requests with photos are usually the quickest to price, and we will tell you if anything is missing.

Nothing is booked until you give job approval. Once you accept the powder coating quote, we confirm drop-off or pickup, reserve oven time and send the timeline in writing. If anything about the part changes after approval, tell us and we will update your quote before work begins, so the final invoice always matches what you agreed.
What Affects the Price

Five price factors shape every powder coating quote: the size of the part, the prep it needs, the quantity, the colour and finish, and the amount of masking. Two parts that look alike can cost different amounts for these reasons.

That is why your quote is always written for your exact part. Heavy rust or old coatings add blasting or stripping time. Large items use more oven space, while a batch of matching parts spreads setup across many pieces. Special colours or textures can cost more than stock shades, and detailed masking takes extra labour. For typical price ranges and what drives them, read our guide to [powder coating cost](/post/how-much-does-powder-coating-cost-ontario). Customers with steady volume can ask about repeat order pricing through [commercial powder coating](/services/bulk-commercial-orders).
Book a Consultation

If your project is complex or you are unsure what finish you need, book a consultation instead of filling in the form. A short call or shop visit before your powder coating quote lets us look at the part with you and recommend prep, powder and colour.

Consultations run Monday to Friday, 7 AM to 5 PM, by phone or at our Milton shop. Bring the part or a sample if you can. For size limits on very large items, see [large part powder coating](/capabilities) before you visit, and for colour ideas, browse [custom powder coating colours](/services/custom-colors-finishes). You will leave with a clear next step and, in most cases, a powder coating estimate. Facilities managers and engineers often use this option before a tender or a plant shutdown.
Powder Coating Quote FAQs
Short answer: send what you have and we will fill the gaps with you. These answers cover photos, dates and missing details, and they are written for this page only, not repeated from other pages.

blocks.q: Can I get a price from photos alone?
blocks.a: Often, yes. Clear photos plus measurements and a quantity are enough for a powder coating quote on most standard parts. For complex or very heavy items, we may ask for a drawing or a sample part first.

Requested start and finish dates are not guaranteed until we confirm them. Once you approve the job, we give you a timeline in writing with your quote for powder coating and plan around your desired finish date.

blocks.q: What if I don't know the metal or colour?
blocks.a: That is fine. Describe the part and how it will be used, and we will help you choose. Leave the colour blank and we can suggest options when we send the price.
